claims.claim: The brigatinib context, which shares a piperazine-containing amino-heteroaryl motif with the query, reports approximate absolute oral bioavailability of 46% after a single 180 mg oral dose in healthy volunteers.
The same scaffold shows absolute oral bioavailability of 57% in the fasted state and 77% after a meal for the 1500 mg tablet, supporting high F across prandial conditions.
Paliperidone, a pyrido-pyrimidinone-type heterocycle with an N-substituent, has absolute oral bioavailability of 28% in fasting volunteers and 28% for the ER formulation, above the 20% threshold.
Other reference contexts (linezolid, encainide, rifapentine, ketanserin) report oral bioavailability values of 49-100%, all above the threshold, providing no affirmative evidence for F < 20%.

evidence_gaps: No direct oral bioavailability record for the query molecule itself is present in the supplied cards.

The closest structural context (C07) has a source-native record naming tacrolimus, creating uncertainty about whether its 20-25% value applies to the displayed scaffold; it is therefore not used as a primary basis.
No matched oral-versus-IV exposure data for the query are available, and prandial-state or formulation effects for the query are unknown.
The low neutral fraction and high TPSA are physicochemical priors only; no experimental permeability or solubility data for the query were supplied.
content.decision_summary: Multiple transferable reference contexts with related heteroaromatic/piperazine scaffolds report absolute oral bioavailability above 20% (28-77%), and no affirmative threshold-relevant evidence supports F < 20%; therefore predict high despite an unfavorable physicochemical prior.
